tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P0] Make feedProjector's closeTurn idempotent so a multi-result turn emits one turn_end
tasks.description:
`feedProjector` in `apps/server/src/services/session/session-event-normalizer.ts` calls `closeTurn()` on EVERY `done` event it sees (the `if (event.type === 'done') { closeTurn(); ended = true; continue; }` branch around line 636), and its `finally` calls it again when the stream ended without one. There is no guard against `closeTurn()` running twice, so a stream carrying two `done` events ingests two `turn_end` events into the projector for one logical turn.

This never fires today because the claude-code runtime maps exactly one SDK `result` per turn: `sdk-event-mapper.ts` routes `result` to `mapResultEvent`, and `event-mappers/result-event-mapper.ts` unconditionally yields `{ type: 'done' }` at the end of that branch (around line 227). One query, one result, one done. It fires immediately once a query stays open across turns, which is what the persistent pump does, so it is a latent blocker for every later phase as well as a bug on its own merits.

What to build: introduce a guard so `closeTurn()` ingests at most one `turn_end` per `feedProjector` call. The existing `ended` flag is close but is set only in the `done` branch and consulted only in the `finally`; make `closeTurn` itself the thing that checks and sets, so both call sites are covered by one rule. Keep the existing `terminalReason` resolution intact: an explicit reason from `session_status`/`done` still wins, and the `sawError` latch still fills an undefined reason with 'error'. The FIRST close is the one that counts; a second `done` must be a no-op, not an overwrite, because the second one carries no reason that belongs to this turn.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A scripted StreamEvent sequence containing two `done` events produces exactly ONE `turn_end` on the projector.
2. A stream that ends without any `done` still produces exactly one `turn_end` from the `finally` (unchanged behavior).
3. A stream with one `done` followed by nothing produces exactly one `turn_end` and the `finally` does not add a second (unchanged behavior).
4. terminalReason resolution is unchanged: explicit reason wins; typed `error` with no explicit reason still closes as `terminalReason: 'error'`.
5. The test is proved able to fail: remove the guard, watch the double-`done` case go red, restore it. Record that in the PR description.
6. The existing server test suite is green with no other file touched.

No feature flag. This is a pure correctness fix and reverts by `git revert`.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P1] Track DOR-1088 turn serialization landing and verify its four guarantees
tasks.description:
TRACKING TASK. No new implementation work. DOR-1088 is being implemented on `worktree-dor-1088-stream-serialize` and must land before phase 2 dispatch work begins. This task exists so the dependency is explicit and verifiable rather than assumed.

What DOR-1088 lands (read from that branch): a new `apps/server/src/services/session/turn-queue.ts` exporting `SessionTurnQueue.reserve(sessionId, clientId) -> TurnSlot { ready, release }`, a per-(session, client) promise chain in the same shape as `RuntimeAdapter.enqueueForSession` (ADR-0075). `trigger-turn.ts` reserves the slot before anything else and awaits `slot.ready`, releasing it inside `releaseOnce` and on the launch-throw path. `session-lock.ts`'s `acquireLock` refuses ANY live lock including the same client's, which removes the same-client re-acquire that let one browser tab start a second turn beside its own. `message-sender.ts`'s `finally` clears `session.activeQuery` only when the frame still owns it.

What this task does: when DOR-1088 merges, verify the four guarantees below hold on `main`, then unblock the dependent tasks. If any fails, raise it on the DOR-1088 work item rather than patching it here.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Two triggers from the SAME client on one session run strictly in sequence: the second turn's `turn_start` is ingested only after the first turn's lock has been released.
2. A second, DIFFERENT client still gets the unchanged answer: 409 SESSION_LOCKED naming the holder while the turn is alive, and an accepted takeover once the holder's lock has expired past its inactivity TTL.
3. `session.activeQuery` is cleared only by the frame that installed it; a late-settling frame does not strand its successor with `activeQuery: undefined`.
4. A throw before the turn is launched (e.g. context assembly failing) releases BOTH the write lock and the queue slot, so the session is not wedged for that client.

Note for phase 2: DOR-1088's chain is in-memory, per-client, invisible to other windows, lost on restart, and holds an HTTP socket open per waiting message. Task 2.3 keeps it as the intra-process ordering primitive and builds the durable queue above it; it is not replaced and it is not the server queue.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P2] Add the disposition and queue types to shared, plus the three capability flags declared false everywhere
tasks.description:
Land the whole type surface first, with no behavior change, so every later task compiles against a settled contract.

In `packages/shared/src/agent-runtime.ts` add:
- `export type MessageDisposition = 'queue' | 'steer' | 'stage'` with TSDoc stating that it is ignored when the session is idle (every disposition then means run it now) and that it defaults to 'queue' at every ingress.
- `export type DispositionDowngradeReason = 'unsupported' | 'session-idle' | 'no-open-turn' | 'pending-interaction'`.
- `export interface MessageDeliveryOutcome { messageId: string; requested: MessageDisposition; applied: MessageDisposition; degradedBecause?: DispositionDowngradeReason }`.
- `export interface QueuedMessage { id: string; content: string; disposition: MessageDisposition; enqueuedAt: number; enqueuedBy: string }`.
- Two optional fields on `MessageOpts`: `disposition?: MessageDisposition` and `messageId?: string`. The `messageId` TSDoc must state that correlation is by id and NEVER positional, because the SDK coalesces a dequeued batch into one turn and several dispatched ids can therefore share one `result`.
- Three REQUIRED booleans on `RuntimeCapabilities`: `supportsPersistentSession`, `supportsSteer`, `supportsContextStaging`. Required rather than optional, following the `commandIntents` and `settings` precedent (ADR-0256), so no adapter can silently omit one. There is deliberately no `supportsQueue`: the server always owns the queue, so every runtime supports queueing by construction.

In `packages/shared/src/session-stream.ts` add the `queue_update` member to the `SessionEvent` union: `{ type: 'queue_update'; seq: number; queue: QueuedMessage[]; outcome?: MessageDeliveryOutcome }`. The whole queue every time, never a diff: it is small and bounded, and full replacement makes ordering and dedup bugs unrepresentable. Add `queuedMessages: QueuedMessage[]` to `SessionSnapshot`.

Add Zod schemas for every new type alongside the existing ones in `packages/shared/src/schemas.ts` / `session-stream.ts`, matching how the neighbouring event members are validated.

Declare all three capability flags as `false` on all four runtimes: `claude-code/runtime-constants.ts`, `codex/runtime-constants.ts`, `opencode/runtime-constants.ts`, and the test-mode capabilities object. Also update `packages/test-utils/src/fake-agent-runtime.ts` if it carries a capabilities literal.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `pnpm --filter @dorkos/shared typecheck` and the full server typecheck pass; the required flags force a compile error if any adapter omits one (verify by deleting one flag from one adapter and seeing it fail).
2. `queue_update` is added to the CLIENT event allowlist in the same PR. A new SessionEvent member that is not allowlisted is dropped silently, and that has bitten this repo before. Include a test asserting a `queue_update` survives the client's event handling path.
3. Existing conformance suites are green: the capability-shape assertions accept the three new booleans.
4. No behavior change: no route, dispatcher, or adapter logic is touched.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P2] Build the durable queue store: Drizzle table, migration, and repository
tasks.description:
Create the persisted queue that makes a typed message survive a refresh, a second window, a failed turn, and a server restart.

Add a table in `packages/db` beside `session_metadata`, with a Drizzle migration:

| column | type | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | text, primary key | the `messageId`, a server-minted uuid |
| `session_id` | text, indexed | canonical session id |
| `position` | integer | SPARSE ordering (e.g. steps of 1000) so a reorder is an UPDATE of one row, not a rewrite of all of them |
| `content` | text | the person's words, pristine; context never mutates it |
| `disposition` | text | 'queue' / 'steer' / 'stage' as REQUESTED, not as applied |
| `client_id` | text | who enqueued it, so a window can tell its own from another's |
| `enqueued_at` | integer | epoch ms |
| `context_json` | text, nullable | the `ClientContext` captured at enqueue time |

Build a repository module (suggested `apps/server/src/services/session/message-queue-store.ts`) exposing: `enqueue`, `list(sessionId)` ordered by position, `remove(id)`, `updateContent(id, content)`, `move(id, beforeId | afterId)` using sparse positions with a renumber fallback when the gap closes, `clear(sessionId)` returning the removed rows (Stop needs them back, see 4.7), and `rekeySession(fromId, toId)`.

`rekeySession` is load-bearing and easy to miss: a brand-new session gains its canonical SDK id mid-first-turn, and every row keyed by the request UUID must move with it. The existing rebind already moves the `session_metadata` row; this join that move. A queue left behind at the old key is invisible forever.

Sweeping: rows whose session no longer exists are removed by the same health check that evicts sessions, so an abandoned session cannot accumulate queue rows for the life of the install.

Why persist at all: ADR-0264 accepts losing an in-flight TURN on restart. Losing a message somebody typed and was told was accepted is a different and worse promise to break. DOR-480 already established that this class of loss is unacceptable, which is why the client queue carries a `restore` handle today.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Enqueue, list, remove, edit, reorder, and clear all round-trip through SQLite with correct ordering.
2. A reorder is a single-row UPDATE while sparse gaps remain; the renumber fallback is exercised by a test that closes a gap.
3. `rekeySession(from, to)` moves every row and is idempotent when the ids match or the source has no rows.
4. `clear(sessionId)` returns the rows it removed, in order.
5. The migration applies cleanly to an existing dev database with sessions in it, and is keyed to a version strictly greater than the newest released `v*` tag.
6. No route or dispatcher is wired yet; this task is storage only.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P2] Build the dispatcher as the single ingress, and audit every trigger caller through it
tasks.description:
The dispatcher is where a message stops being a request and becomes a turn. It is the one place that decides whether to run now, queue, or degrade, and every caller that can start a turn must go through it or that caller keeps the old race.

Build it (suggested `apps/server/src/services/session/message-dispatcher.ts`) with these rules:
1. Accept a message with a requested disposition; mint a `messageId`; write the row via the store from task 2.2; return a `MessageDeliveryOutcome` plus the queue position.
2. Resolve the disposition against the resolved runtime's capabilities and the session's live state. In THIS phase every disposition resolves to 'queue' (the capability flags are all false from task 2.1), so `steer` and `stage` come back as `applied: 'queue', degradedBecause: 'unsupported'`. The ladder's shape lands now; its native branches land in phase 4.
3. Dispatch the head of the queue when a turn ends. Dequeue on `turn_end`, NEVER on a bare `result`: premature dequeue is a known failure in every queue-capable tool (OpenCode #15696) and dequeuing on `result` is exactly how you get it.
4. Never dispatch while `projector.hasPendingInteractions()` is true. That probe already exists and is already shared by the write lock and the stall watchdog in `trigger-turn.ts`; reuse it rather than inventing a third liveness notion. Firing a queued prompt into an open permission ask is the other known failure (Gemini #17719, OpenCode #2609).
5. Order by `position`, FIFO within a position.
6. Keep DOR-1088's `SessionTurnQueue` as the intra-process ordering primitive underneath. It is not replaced. What changes is that the HTTP request no longer waits on it (task 2.4).
7. Dispatch and reap share the dispatch mutex, so a reap racing a dispatch simply does not happen. (The reaper arrives in phase 3; leave the seam.)

Audit and migrate every existing trigger caller to route through the dispatcher: `routes/sessions.ts` (the message POST), `routes/session-ui-action-handler.ts`, `routes/session-command-intent-handler.ts`, `services/rooms/room-turn-runner.ts`, `services/session/embedded-turn-trigger.ts` (two call sites), `services/tasks/run-stream.ts`, and `services/mesh/mcp-signin-resume.ts`. Note that claude-code's `executeCommandIntent` is literally `sendMessage('/compact')`, so command intents contend identically and go through the dispatcher too.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A message sent to a BUSY session is accepted and queued; it dispatches automatically when the running turn's `turn_end` lands.
2. A message sent to an IDLE session runs immediately, with `applied: 'queue', requested: 'queue'` and no degradation notice.
3. A queued message does NOT dispatch while a pending interaction is open, and DOES dispatch once that interaction is resolved.
4. A queued message behind a turn that FAILS still dispatches; a failed turn does not eat the queue.
5. The caller audit is a TEST, not a claim: assert that no module outside the dispatcher calls `runtime.sendMessage` or `runtime.executeCommandIntent` for a person-initiated turn (an import-graph or grep-based guard test in the same shape as the existing SDK-confinement checks).
6. `steer` and `stage` requests return `applied: 'queue'` with `degradedBecause: 'unsupported'`.
tasks.activeForm: Building the dispatcher as the single ingress

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P2] Retire 409 from the message POST and add the queue routes
tasks.description:
Change what `POST /api/sessions/:id/messages` means, and give the queue an HTTP surface.

The POST accepts an optional `disposition` in the body, defaulting to 'queue'. It returns 202 IMMEDIATELY with `{ sessionId, messageId, outcome, queuePosition }`. Two behaviors go away with this change:
- The 409 SESSION_LOCKED answer on the message path. A busy session is no longer a refusal; it is a queue.
- DOR-1088's interim behavior of holding the HTTP socket open until the queued turn actually starts. The 202 now resolves at acceptance, and the client learns the turn started from the durable stream like everything else.

The canonical-id contract is unchanged: the 202's `sessionId` is still best effort, resolved by tapping the runtime's stream with a 5-second bound, and it still converges later via the retire announce.

Add:
- `GET /api/sessions/:id/queue` returning the queue. Redundant with the snapshot on purpose, and worth having for integrations and debugging.
- `PATCH /api/sessions/:id/queue/:messageId` to edit content or move position.
- `DELETE /api/sessions/:id/queue/:messageId` to remove one.

The write lock survives, retargeted. It stops being 'who may POST' and becomes the internal dispatch mutex held for one turn window. Its inactivity-TTL machinery (`LockActivity`, DOR-782) is unchanged and is still what reclaims a dark turn, so a crashed holder still frees its session.

Rewrite clause 3 of `apps/server/src/routes/__tests__/sessions-cross-client.test.ts`. That test's own header already says this is coming: 'DOR-82 will replace this incidental semantics with explicit queue/steer/interrupt dispositions'. It currently asserts 409-while-alive and takeover-once-dark on the message path. It becomes: a second client's mid-turn POST is ACCEPTED (202) and queued, both clients see the same queue on their streams, and the message runs when the first turn ends. Preserve the DOR-782 lesson in the rewritten comment so the next reader does not re-derive it.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A POST to a busy session returns 202 with a `messageId` and a queue position. There is NO code path on the message route that returns 409 SESSION_LOCKED.
2. The POST returns without waiting for the turn ahead of it: measure that the response settles while the prior turn is still streaming.
3. Queue GET/PATCH/DELETE work and reject unknown ids with 404 and malformed ids with 400, matching the route conventions already in that file.
4. `sessions-cross-client.test.ts` clause 3 asserts accept-and-queue and is green.
5. A second client can remove or edit a message the FIRST client queued; the queue is per session, not per client.
6. Express 5 semantics respected: an empty POST body leaves `req.body` undefined and is rejected as a 400, not a crash.
tasks.activeForm: Retiring 409 and adding the queue routes

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P2] Surface the queue on the snapshot and the durable stream, and rehydrate it after restart
tasks.description:
Make the queue visible to every window through the mechanism ADR-0264 already provides, and make it come back after a restart.

Wire `SessionStateProjector` (`apps/server/src/services/session/session-state-projector.ts`) so that:
1. `getSessionSnapshot` includes `queuedMessages`, read from the store, so a cold connect sees the queue in the same payload as messages, status, and pending interactions. A client that has just hydrated must never have to make a second request to know what is queued.
2. Every queue mutation (enqueue, edit, reorder, remove, dispatch, clear) emits a `queue_update` event carrying the WHOLE queue and, when the update was caused by an accepted message, the `MessageDeliveryOutcome`. The event takes a `seq` like any other, so the client's existing idempotent-apply-by-seq logic covers it with no new rules.
3. On projector creation for a session that has queue rows on disk, the queue is loaded so a post-restart snapshot is correct. This is the restart half of the durability promise and it is easy to forget: the rows survive, but a projector that never reads them reports an empty queue and the dispatcher never fires.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A cold `GET /api/sessions/:id/events` connect returns a snapshot whose `queuedMessages` matches the store exactly, in order.
2. Enqueueing from window A produces a `queue_update` on window B's stream within the normal event latency, carrying the full queue.
3. Removing from window B produces a `queue_update` on window A.
4. A `queue_update` caused by a degraded acceptance carries the outcome with `requested`, `applied`, and `degradedBecause` populated.
5. Server restart with three messages queued: after restart, a cold connect's snapshot shows all three in the original order, and they dispatch normally when a turn ends.
6. Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` still replays gap-free with `queue_update` events in the sequence; the epoch check and the `StaleResumeCursorError` fallback are unaffected.
tasks.activeForm: Surfacing the queue on the snapshot and stream

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P2] Cut the cockpit over from the local queue to the server queue, preserving every affordance
tasks.description:
Replace the client-owned queue (ADR-0104) with a view of the server's, without losing a single thing the composer can do today.

The current implementation is `apps/client/src/layers/features/chat/model/use-message-queue.ts` plus `use-chat-queue.ts` and the session-entity queue store. It is ephemeral React state: lost on refresh, invisible to a second window, and flushed on the streaming-to-idle edge. What it gets RIGHT and must be preserved exactly:
- Queue chips with edit-in-place, keyed by a stable `editingId` that survives queue mutations rather than a positional cursor.
- Reorder and remove.
- Send-now.
- The `restore` handle. It exists because a refused trigger once destroyed a person's typed words (DOR-480). In the server world the equivalent promise is that a failed enqueue puts the text back in the composer rather than dropping it.

What changes: the queue is read from the session snapshot and kept current by `queue_update` events; mutations go to the queue routes; the streaming-to-idle auto-flush disappears entirely because the server dispatches. Delete the local FIFO and its auto-flush effect rather than leaving it dormant. Two queues means two sources of truth and a reconciliation bug waiting to happen.

Also surface, quietly: a chip queued by another window is visibly not this window's (the `enqueuedBy` field carries the client id). It stays fully editable; it just does not pretend to be yours.

The degradation notice slot lands here but stays unused until phase 4: when an outcome carries `degradedBecause`, the chip can say what happened. The one case that must stay SILENT is `degradedBecause: 'session-idle'`, because 'it ran immediately' is not a degradation anybody needs told.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Type three messages while the agent works: all three appear as chips, survive a hard refresh, and appear in a second window.
2. Edit a chip in window A; window B shows the edit.
3. Remove a chip in window B; window A's list updates.
4. Reorder in either window; both agree on the order and the dispatch order matches.
5. When the turn ends, the head dispatches automatically and its chip disappears in both windows.
6. A failed enqueue (network down) returns the text to the composer; nothing typed is lost.
7. `use-message-queue.ts`'s local FIFO and its auto-flush effect are DELETED, not left dormant. Knip reports no orphaned queue code.
8. Every existing queue test either migrates to the server-backed behavior or is deleted with its reason recorded; none is left asserting the old local semantics.
tasks.activeForm: Cutting the cockpit over to the server queue

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P2] Write ADR-c (server-owned durable message queue), supersede ADR-0104, and update the integration docs
tasks.description:
Record the decision and tell integrators what changed.

Write the ADR at `decisions/<timestamp-id>-server-owned-durable-message-queue.md` using an id from `.claude/scripts/id.ts`, and add its `decisions/manifest.json` entry. Content:
- Context: the queue lived in the browser as ephemeral React state (ADR-0104), lost on refresh, invisible to a second window, with a `409 SESSION_LOCKED` refusal standing in for coordination between clients.
- Decision: the server owns the queue, persisted, keyed by canonical session id, surfaced on the snapshot and the durable stream, mutable from any window. Native runtime queuing stays an adapter-level optimization and never the contract.
- This AMENDS ADR-0264 by naming the queue as the thing that sits behind the trigger-only POST, which ADR-0264's own context anticipated but did not build.
- This SUPERSEDES ADR-0104. Edit ADR-0104's front matter to set `superseded-by` and add a line explaining what replaced it and why (durability and multi-window, not dissatisfaction with the original design, which was correct for its time).
- Consequences, honestly including the negative: a persisted queue is a migration and a new sweep obligation, and the 202 now means 'accepted' rather than 'running', which is a real semantic change for any integrator polling on it.

Update `docs/integrations/sse-protocol.mdx`: the `queue_update` event, the `queuedMessages` snapshot field, and the retirement of 409 from the message POST. This file is the public integration contract, so the change must be described from an integrator's point of view, not the implementation's.

Add a changelog fragment in `changelog/unreleased/` (`<timestamp-id>-<slug>.md`) written per the `writing-for-humans` standard: plain enough for a smart 9th grader who does not code. Describe what happens for the person ('messages you type while an agent is working now wait safely on the server, so they survive a refresh and show up in every window'), never the mechanism.

Acceptance criteria:
1. ADR-c exists with a timestamp id, is registered in `decisions/manifest.json`, and follows the repo's ADR shape (Status / Context / Decision / Consequences with Positive and Negative).
2. ADR-0104's front matter carries `superseded-by` pointing at ADR-c.
3. `docs/integrations/sse-protocol.mdx` documents `queue_update`, `queuedMessages`, and the 409 retirement.
4. A changelog fragment exists and passes the `fragment-present` CI gate.
5. No user-facing copy uses hype language or describes internals.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P3] Adopt the push()-capable held prompt into sdk-utils as the pump's input seam
tasks.description:
Convert the held streaming-input prompt from a one-shot into a queue-driven generator that can accept more messages while it is open. This is the seam the whole pump grows out of, and it can land independently and early.

Today `createHeldPrompt` in `apps/server/src/services/runtimes/claude-code/sdk/sdk-utils.ts` yields each of its `messages` and then parks on a single `held` promise until `close()` resolves it. It cannot accept anything after construction.

The DOR-1087 branch (`worktree-dor-1087-phantom-stop`) has ALREADY written this conversion: the generator drains an internal queue, parks on a `wake` promise, and `push(content)` appends and wakes it, returning `false` once closed. ADOPT THAT IMPLEMENTATION rather than writing a second one, and coordinate with whoever is finishing DOR-1087 so the two do not diverge into subtly different generators. If DOR-1087 has landed by the time this task starts, this task is a no-op verification; if it has not, lift the conversion and let DOR-1087 rebase onto it.

The contract to land:
- `HeldUserPrompt` gains `push(content: string): boolean` documented as: the CLI queues the message and delivers it at its next opportunity within the live turn; returns false and sends nothing once `close()` has been called.
- `close()` stays idempotent and still terminates the generator so the subprocess drains and exits.
- `createIdlePrompt()` (zero messages, an intentional idle probe used to read a session's command set at zero token cost) keeps working unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `push` before the generator is consumed, and `push` while it is parked, both deliver in FIFO order.
2. `push` after `close` returns `false` and yields nothing.
3. `close` is idempotent and always terminates the generator, including when the queue is non-empty at close time (define and TEST the chosen behavior: drain-then-close is the recommendation, so nothing already accepted is silently dropped).
4. `createIdlePrompt()` still yields nothing and still holds the stream open.
5. Existing `sdk-utils.test.ts` cases are green, plus new cases for each behavior above.
6. No caller behavior changes yet: `message-sender.ts` still uses one message and closes on the first `result`.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P3] Build the SessionPump: state machine, warmth reporting, and launch/teardown
tasks.description:
Create the long-lived process owner. New module `apps/server/src/services/runtimes/claude-code/sessions/session-pump.ts`, inside the claude-code adapter so the SDK stays confined there (Hard Rule 2).

The pump owns: the long-lived `query()`, its held input stream (from task 3.1), the demux of its output, the idle timer (task 3.4), and the crash detector (task 3.6). `executeSdkQuery` stops being 'the turn' and becomes the pump's launcher.

States and transitions to implement exactly:

| From | To | Trigger | Guard | Side effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| COLD | WARMING | first dispatch or explicit warm | under the warm ceiling | `query()` with `resume` when `hasStarted`, else fresh |
| WARMING | WARM | `system/init` received | | capabilities feature-detected and cached; control methods usable |
| WARMING | CRASHED | exit or throw before init | | dispatch fails over to RESUMING once |
| WARM | RUNNING | dispatch | dispatch mutex held; no pending interaction | `turn_start` ingested; stall watchdog armed |
| RUNNING | WARM | correlated `result` | | one `turn_end`; watchdog disarmed; idle timer armed; queue head dequeued |
| RUNNING | CRASHED | exit or throw mid-turn | | open window closed with `turn_end{terminalReason:'error'}`; queue preserved |
| WARM | REAPED | idle timer or LRU eviction | no open turn AND no pending interaction | `close()` on the held stream |
| any | COLD | session eviction | | reap first, then drop the session record |
| CRASHED | RESUMING | next dispatch | | fresh `query()` with `resume`: today's path exactly |
| RESUMING | WARMING | `query()` returns | | |

Add to `AgentRuntime` in `packages/shared/src/agent-runtime.ts`, both OPTIONAL so runtimes with no warm concept simply omit them:
- `export type SessionWarmth = 'cold' | 'warming' | 'warm' | 'running' | 'crashed'`
- `getSessionWarmth?(sessionId: string): SessionWarmth`
- `reapSession?(sessionId: string): Promise<void>` documented as: closes the warm process without touching the session record or its transcript; idempotent; a no-op when not warm; NEVER called while a pending interaction is open.

Capability feature detection: read the `capabilities` array from `system/init` and cache it per pump. Feature-detect, never version-sniff; the SDK's own docs instruct this, and it is what lets an older CLI degrade honestly instead of crashing.

Wire teardown into `shutdownServices()` in `apps/server/src/index.ts` so no warm subprocess survives DorkOS. The OpenCode sidecar teardown (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace window, no-op when never booted) is the model.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Every transition in the table is unit-tested by driving the pump directly, including the guards (a dispatch is refused while a pending interaction is open; a warm is refused over the ceiling).
2. `getSessionWarmth` returns the state the machine is actually in at each point, and `'cold'` for an unknown id.
3. `reapSession` is idempotent and a no-op when cold.
4. `shutdownServices()` leaves zero orphan subprocesses; assert by process inspection in an integration test.
5. Nothing is wired to the dispatcher yet, and the flag is off by default, so this task changes no runtime behavior.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P3] Window the pump's output into turns, correlated by messageId
tasks.description:
Turn the pump's single continuous output into the discrete turns the durable stream expects.

The rule: a DorkOS turn OPENS on dispatch and CLOSES on the `result` that answers it.

Today the units coincide, which is why nothing needed windowing: one `sendMessage` equals one `query()` equals one `result` equals one `done` equals one `turn_end`. With a pump they come apart, and the CLI can also start continuations DorkOS never asked for (auto-resume continuations are named in the SDK's own `still_queued` documentation).

Implement:
1. Each dispatch stamps its `SDKUserMessage` with the server-minted `messageId` as the message `uuid` and opens a turn window.
2. A `result` is correlated back to the window by that id. Correlation is by id and NEVER positional: the SDK coalesces a dequeued batch into ONE turn, so several dispatched ids can share one `result`. Text matching was already rejected for this exact ambiguity when the room runner needed turn identity; do not reintroduce it.
3. On the correlated `result`, close the window: exactly one `turn_end`, with `terminalReason` resolved by the existing rules. Task 0.1's idempotence guard is what makes a second `result` harmless rather than a second close.
4. A `result` with NO correlated `messageId` opens a synthetic turn tagged `origin: 'runtime'`. It is not dropped and it is not disguised as a person's turn. The durable stream must stay a complete account of the session; this is the same honesty rule the presence contract already enforces on every runtime.
5. `session.contextBreakdown` and the subscription-usage fetch currently happen once, at the first `result`, immediately before `heldPrompt.close()`. They must now happen per window close, WITHOUT closing the stream.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Three dispatches through one pump produce exactly three `turn_start`/`turn_end` pairs on the durable stream, in order, with no overlap.
2. A coalesced batch (two dispatched ids, one `result`) closes BOTH windows correctly rather than leaving one open forever.
3. An uncorrelated `result` produces a turn tagged `origin: 'runtime'` and is visible on the stream.
4. `context_usage` is emitted before `done` within every window, not just the first.
5. The subprocess is still alive after a window closes: `getSessionWarmth` reports `'warm'`, and a control method (e.g. `getContextUsage`) still answers.
6. Killing the process mid-window closes that window with `turn_end{terminalReason:'error'}` and exactly one of them.
tasks.activeForm: Windowing the pump output into turns

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P3] Add the process idle timer and the warm-session LRU ceiling
tasks.description:
Bound how long a warm process lives and how many exist at once. These are two DIFFERENT timers from session eviction, and conflating them is the trap this task exists to avoid.

Add to `apps/server/src/config/constants.ts` under `SESSIONS`:
- `WARM_IDLE_MS: 5 * 60 * 1000` with a TSDoc explaining it governs WARM to REAPED (how long a live subprocess sits with no turn open) and is NOT session eviction. Long enough that a person thinking between turns keeps their cache; short enough that abandoned sessions do not hold subprocesses.
- `MAX_WARM_SESSIONS: 12` with a TSDoc explaining it counts PROCESSES, while the existing `MAX_SESSIONS: 50` counts session RECORDS. Warmth is a cache, so it is LRU-evicted down to the ceiling regardless of the idle timer. Records stay at 50 so `ensureSession`'s existing throw stays the genuinely exceptional path it is today.

Implement in the pump registry:
1. The idle timer arms when a turn window closes and disarms on the next dispatch. On fire: reap.
2. LRU eviction: when a new pump would exceed `MAX_WARM_SESSIONS`, reap the least recently used WARM pump first.
3. REAP IS FORBIDDEN while `projector.hasPendingInteractions()` is true. `INTERACTION_TIMEOUT_MS` is 10 minutes, LONGER than the 5-minute idle window, so this is not a theoretical race: a person can walk away from an approval card and have the reaper fire under them, and a reaped process cannot answer the approval they come back to. Reuse the existing probe; do not invent a third liveness notion.
4. Reap is forbidden while a turn window is open, enforced by the shared dispatch mutex so a reap racing a dispatch simply does not happen.
5. Hook the sweep into the existing `checkSessionHealth` cadence (`INTERVALS.HEALTH_CHECK_MS`, 5 minutes) rather than adding another interval. Session eviction continues to imply reap; reap never implies eviction.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A warm session with no dispatch for `WARM_IDLE_MS` is reaped; `getSessionWarmth` goes to `'cold'` and the subprocess exits.
2. A warm session with a PENDING INTERACTION open is NOT reaped, even well past `WARM_IDLE_MS`; it is reaped once the interaction resolves and the window closes.
3. Warming a 13th session with `MAX_WARM_SESSIONS: 12` reaps the least recently used one first; the session RECORD count is unaffected and stays bounded by 50.
4. Session eviction at `TIMEOUT_MS` reaps the pump before dropping the record; no subprocess outlives its session record.
5. A reap and a dispatch racing on the same session cannot interleave: assert with a deterministic scheduling test, not a sleep.
6. Both new constants have TSDoc that names what they are NOT, so the next reader does not conflate them.
tasks.activeForm: Adding the idle timer and warm ceiling

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P3] Implement the relaunch pin list, including the unconditional account pin
tasks.description:
A warm process pins whatever it was launched with. Any change to a pinned value must force a reap and relaunch, or the next turn runs under stale settings. This is the highest-severity task in the phase: getting the account row wrong bills a paying client's conversation to the wrong account.

Today every one of these is resolved PER TURN inside `executeSdkQuery`. On a pump they are resolved once, at launch, so each needs a decision and an enforcement point.

Must force a REAP AND RELAUNCH when changed:
- `cwd` (the effective working directory resolved from message opts, session cwd, then default).
- The Claude account root, i.e. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` from `claudeConfigDirEnv(session.accountRoot ?? resolveActiveClaudeRoot())`. UNCONDITIONAL. A session's transcript exists under exactly one account and only that account may resume it and bill for it.
- The resolved credential env from `resolveClaudeCredentialEnv()` (ADR-0315). A revoked credential must not keep working because the process that holds it launched before the revocation.
- The agent identity token from `resolveAgentTokenEnv(...)`.
- The system-prompt append (built from the agent manifest's tool-group settings plus any caller-supplied append).
- `settingSources` and the process `env` block generally.

Must NOT force a relaunch; mutate the live query instead:
- `mcpServers`: use `setMcpServers` on the live query.
- `plugins`: use `reload_plugins`, which is already wired for the live-session propagation path.
- `permissionMode`: use `setPermissionMode`. Keep the existing auto-to-default coercion guard for models that do not support auto, and keep it a per-dispatch coercion that never mutates the stored preference.
- `model` / `effort` / `fastMode`: use `setModel` where the SDK genuinely supports the change on a live query, and relaunch otherwise. VERIFY PER FIELD against the live SDK during this task; do not assume all three behave alike, and record what you verified in the adapter's `NOTES.md` alongside the other live-verified facts.

Implementation shape: compute a launch fingerprint from the must-relaunch set, store it on the pump, and compare on every dispatch. A mismatch reaps and relaunches BEFORE the turn opens, transparently to the person.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Each must-relaunch value, changed between two dispatches, causes exactly one reap-and-relaunch and the second turn observes the new value.
2. The ACCOUNT case has a dedicated test that would otherwise bill the wrong account: a session whose `accountRoot` differs from the active root must launch under its own, and a change must relaunch.
3. Each live-mutable value, changed between two dispatches, causes NO relaunch and is observed by the second turn.
4. The per-field `setModel` verdicts are recorded in `claude-code/NOTES.md` with what was verified and how.
5. A relaunch preserves the queue and the session record; only the process is replaced.
6. Boundary validation is not in this task (see 3.9) but the fingerprint must not be mistaken for it: a fingerprint match is not a boundary check.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P3] Detect process death and fall back to the resume path with the queue intact
tasks.description:
Make the persistent path degrade into the old path instead of failing.

With resume-per-message, a crash cost one turn and the next message trivially restarted. With a pump the blast radius is the SESSION: warm cache, the in-flight turn, and every message queued behind it. The queue surviving a crash is the entire justification for it being server-owned, so this task is where that promise is kept.

Implement:
1. Detect the process ending: subprocess exit, the SDK generator throwing, or the stream closing unexpectedly, both mid-window and while WARM.
2. Mid-window: close the open turn with `turn_end{terminalReason:'error'}` and a typed `error` event carrying the failure, exactly as `guardTurnErrors` does today for a thrown `sendMessage`. The durable stream must show `status_change(error)`, then the typed `error`, then one `turn_end(error)`, and never a frozen `streaming`.
3. PRESERVE THE QUEUE. A crash must not clear it. Queued messages dispatch after recovery.
4. Transition to CRASHED. The next dispatch goes to RESUMING: a fresh `query()` with `resume` set. This is today's path exactly, F1 (`resumeSessionAt` anchoring) and F2 (`isResumeFailure` retry) included, and both are deliberately retained HERE rather than deleted, because this is the recovery route the spec keeps them for.
5. Bound the failover: one automatic resume attempt per crash. A second consecutive crash surfaces as a turn error rather than looping, so a genuinely broken session cannot spin.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Killing the subprocess mid-turn closes that turn with `turn_end{terminalReason:'error'}` and exactly one of them; the session is not left `streaming`.
2. Two messages queued behind the crashed turn are still in the queue afterwards, in order, and dispatch once the session recovers.
3. The next dispatch after a crash resumes the conversation, and the transcript is continuous: the recovered turn sees the prior conversation.
4. A crash while WARM (no turn open) is detected and reported as warmth `'crashed'`, with no spurious turn on the stream: nothing was running, so nothing should appear to have failed.
5. Two consecutive crashes surface an error to the person rather than looping.
6. The resume fallback still applies its anchor and its stale-session retry, unchanged, and the existing tests covering both are green.
tasks.activeForm: Detecting process death and falling back to resume

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P3] Arm and disarm the stall watchdog per turn window instead of per generator
tasks.description:
Stop the stall watchdog from shooting a healthy warm session.

Today `withStallGuard` (composed inside `guardTurnErrors` in `apps/server/src/services/session/trigger-turn.ts`) wraps the whole `sendMessage` generator, which today equals exactly one turn. Its inactivity window is `SESSIONS.TURN_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS`, 10 minutes, and it pauses while the session is parked on a person. On a stall it interrupts the runtime and injects the typed-error terminal sequence.

On a pump the generator spans the PROCESS, not a turn. Left as is, a WARM session sitting legitimately silent for 10 minutes would be interrupted for no reason: the watchdog exists to end a turn that has gone dark, and a warm session is not a turn and has nothing to end.

Implement: arm on turn-window OPEN, disarm on turn-window CLOSE. Silence with no window open is bounded by the idle timer from task 3.4 instead, which is both the right mechanism and shorter anyway (5 minutes versus 10).

Everything else about the guard is unchanged and must stay: the pause while `hasPendingInteractions()` is true, the bounded interrupt (`STALL_INTERRUPT_TIMEOUT_MS`, 30 seconds, so a wedged `interruptQuery` cannot itself hang the thing meant to unstick a hung turn), and the clean stream ending so `feedProjector` settles and the lock releases as on any turn.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A WARM session silent past `TURN_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS` is NOT interrupted; it is reaped by the idle timer instead.
2. A turn window that goes silent past the timeout IS interrupted and closes with the typed-error terminal sequence, exactly as today.
3. A turn parked on a pending interaction is not interrupted for as long as the person takes, bounded by `INTERACTION_TIMEOUT_MS`.
4. The bounded-interrupt path still applies: a wedged interrupt closes the turn anyway after `STALL_INTERRUPT_TIMEOUT_MS`.
5. Existing stall-guard tests pass unchanged where they describe within-turn behavior.
tasks.activeForm: Rearming the stall watchdog per turn window

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P3] Add the per-session opt-in config field and its migration
tasks.description:
Give the persistent path an off switch, defaulting off.

Add a boolean under `runtimes.claudeCode` in `packages/shared/src/config-schema.ts` (suggested `persistentSession`), defaulting `false`, with Zod as the authoritative schema. Then add a semver-keyed backfill to `CONFIG_MIGRATIONS` in `apps/server/src/services/core/config-manager.ts`, following `backfillRuntimesDefaults` as the pattern.

Migration rules that bite if ignored: key the migration to a NEW version strictly greater than the newest `v*` tag (`git tag -l 'v*' | sort -V | tail -1`), and never extend a key that has already shipped. `conf` runs a key only in `(storedVersion, projectVersion]`, so a key at or below a released version, or a body appended to one, never runs for anybody already on it. A guard test compares every key's source text against the newest release and reddens CI if this is wrong.

Why per-session opt-in rather than a global flag: the two paths must run side by side on one host, because that is the only way to compare them on the same workload, and because the resume path is not going away (it is the recovery route). The flag is read at pump launch, so a session that started on one path stays on it until its process is replaced.

Update `contributing/configuration.md` with the new field and what it does.

Acceptance criteria:
1. The field exists in the Zod schema with a `false` default and a TSDoc sentence describing the user-visible effect, not the mechanism.
2. The migration is keyed above the newest release tag and the migration-safety guard is green.
3. With the flag off, claude-code behaves byte-for-byte as it does today: resume-per-message, one process per turn. Assert this with the existing adapter suite unchanged.
4. With the flag on, the pump is used.
5. Two sessions on one host, one with the flag on and one off, both work.
6. `contributing/configuration.md` documents the field.
tasks.activeForm: Adding the opt-in config field and migration

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P3] Move boundary validation from launch to dispatch
tasks.description:
Keep the directory boundary check on the path a cwd can actually change.

`executeSdkQuery` currently calls `validateBoundaryOrDorkHome(effectiveCwd)` at the top of every turn, yielding a typed boundary-violation error and returning when it fails. That is per-turn today because every turn is a fresh launch.

On a pump, launch happens once. If the boundary check moves to launch along with everything else, a cwd change between dispatches would slip past it. The pin list (task 3.5) forces a relaunch on a cwd change, which mostly covers it, but 'mostly' is not the standard for a security boundary: the check must be its own guarantee and not a side effect of a fingerprint comparison.

Implement: run `validateBoundaryOrDorkHome` per DISPATCH, before the turn window opens. On failure, yield the same typed error and do not open a window. Keep the existing carve-out semantics exactly: the agents-subtree seam stays allowed (the system agent and marketplace agents legitimately run outside a narrow boundary), while dork-home siblings such as the credential store and boundary-external paths stay denied.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A dispatch with an out-of-boundary cwd is refused with the existing typed error, and no turn window opens.
2. A session that dispatches in-boundary, then out-of-boundary, is refused on the second dispatch even though the process is already warm.
3. The agents-subtree carve-out still permits a DorkBot or marketplace-agent turn in its own home directory.
4. The credential-store sibling path is still denied.
5. A refused dispatch does not reap or crash the pump; the session stays usable for a subsequent in-boundary message.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P3] Declare supportsPersistentSession and add the warmth conformance cases
tasks.description:
Turn the flag on for claude-code and hold it to the contract.

Set `supportsPersistentSession: true` in `claude-code/runtime-constants.ts`. The other two flags stay `false` until phase 4.

Add to `RuntimeConformanceOpts` in `packages/test-utils/src/runtime-conformance.ts`:

```ts
  /**
   * Drives a session to WARM (a completed turn with the process still held) and
   * hands control back. Provided ONLY by runtimes declaring
   * `supportsPersistentSession`. Omit it and the warmth cases SKIP by name
   * rather than passing on an absence the suite manufactured.
   */
  warmSession?: (runtime: AgentRuntime, sessionId: string) => Promise<void>;
```

Add two cases:
- **C4 warmth honesty.** A runtime declaring `supportsPersistentSession` must report `lifecycle: 'idle'` with `inProgressTurn: null` while WARM. The presence contract already forbids `streaming` with an empty `inProgressTurn` because an empty array is absence wearing the shape of presence; WARM is a NEW way to get that wrong, since the process is alive while nothing is running. The strip omits rather than lies.
- **C5 reap transparency.** Drive to WARM, reap via `reapSession`, dispatch again: the resulting turn is well formed and indistinguishable from one on a warm process. The person cannot tell.

Follow the established driver stance: a case with no driver registers as a NAMED SKIP, never a silent pass. A runtime's `sendMessage` is a pure event producer that moves no projector, so a warmth assertion read off it alone would report the same thing for every runtime and assert nothing.

Acceptance criteria:
1. C4 and C5 are green for claude-code with the flag on, and SKIP by name for codex, opencode, and test-mode (none of which declares the capability yet).
2. C4 is proved able to fail: make the pump report `streaming` while WARM and watch it go red.
3. The existing presence cases stay green; the new cases do not weaken or duplicate them.
4. `contributing/adding-a-runtime.md` documents `supportsPersistentSession`, `getSessionWarmth`, `reapSession`, and the `warmSession` driver, in the same voice as the existing presence section.
5. Ten consecutive turns in one session run on ONE subprocess: assert process identity, not just the absence of an error.
tasks.activeForm: Declaring persistence and adding warmth conformance

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P3] Write ADR-b (persistent streaming-input sessions with resume as the recovery path)
tasks.description:
Record the process-model decision.

Write the ADR at `decisions/<timestamp-id>-persistent-streaming-input-sessions.md` using an id from `.claude/scripts/id.ts`, and add its `decisions/manifest.json` entry. Content:
- Context: claude-code ran resume-per-message plus held-stream-within-turn. Every turn paid a fresh subprocess, a fresh MCP connection, and a cold prompt cache, and the shape produced a family of fragilities: anchor hacking to stop the CLI's resume classifier injecting a synthetic continue turn, substring-matched resume-failure retries that restart a session as new, and a canonical-id rebind that must move every consumer mid-turn.
- Decision: one persistent `query()` per ACTIVE session with WARM as a real state; an idle timer that closes the process; resume DEMOTED to the crash, restart, and cold-start recovery path rather than deleted.
- Record the two-timer model explicitly and why they must not be conflated: process idle (WARM to REAPED, 5 minutes) versus session eviction (30 minutes). Eviction implies reap; reap never implies eviction. Reaping is invisible, which is what makes the short window safe.
- Record the warm ceiling as a SEPARATE number from the session ceiling, and why: warmth is a cache, so it is LRU-rationed, while session records are not.
- Record the relaunch pin list, and name the account pin as a security control rather than an optimization detail.
- Rejected alternative: keep resume-per-message and queue only at our layer. It leaves steering impossible and every turn cold, which is most of the motivation.
- Non-goal recorded deliberately: the process does NOT survive a DorkOS restart. ADR-0264 already accepts in-flight turn loss on restart and the pump inherits that boundary.
- Include the D3 note: the SDK's `priority` field carries no prose documentation even at 0.3.224, so nothing was built on it. 'We measured nothing and therefore relied on nothing' belongs here rather than in an ADR of its own.

Acceptance criteria:
1. ADR-b exists with a timestamp id, is registered in `decisions/manifest.json`, and follows the repo's ADR shape.
2. The two-timer distinction, the warm ceiling rationale, the pin list, and the restart non-goal are all recorded.
3. The rejected alternative is stated with its reason.
4. A changelog fragment exists for the phase and passes the `fragment-present` gate.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P4] Add deliverIntoTurn to AgentRuntime and implement steer for claude-code via streamInput
[persistent-session-runtime] [P4] Implement stage via shouldQuery:false, plus the fold-into-next fallback
tasks.description:
Let a person attach information without provoking a turn.

Implement `mode: 'stage'` for claude-code by sending an `SDKUserMessage` with `shouldQuery: false`. The SDK documents this precisely: the message is appended to the transcript WITHOUT triggering an assistant turn, and it is merged into the next user message that does query. That is exactly the semantics wanted, so the native path is a single field rather than any machinery of ours.

Unlike steer, stage requires NO open turn: it is legal on a warm or even cold session (a cold one warms first, since the message has to reach the transcript).

Build the fallback for runtimes without the capability: hold the text server-side and fold it into the NEXT dispatched message as an `additionalContext` entry. The `queue_note` kind is the precedent for exactly this shape, and it matters that the fallback rides the neutral context bag rather than being concatenated into `content`: injected context must never render as user-authored text, and the adapter strips its tags on render (ADR-0273).

Emit a `context_staged` event so the transcript stays honest. A person who attached a file and saw nothing happen needs some evidence it landed; a silent success is indistinguishable from a dropped message. Add the event to the `SessionEvent` union with a Zod schema AND to the client event allowlist in the same PR.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A staged message on claude-code provokes NO turn: no `turn_start`, no `turn_end`, no model call, no cost.
2. The next dispatched message carries the staged content into the model's context, and the model can act on it.
3. A staged message emits `context_staged` on the durable stream and appears as a quiet transcript entry rather than as a user turn.
4. The fallback path (capability off) folds the text into the next dispatch as an `additionalContext` entry, and the person's `content` for that next message is unmodified.
5. Two staged messages before one dispatch both arrive, in order.
6. Staging on a cold session warms it and works, without running a turn.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P4] Add the turn_input event so a steer renders inside the live turn
tasks.description:
Make a steer visible where it happened.

A steer joins an open turn rather than opening one, so it has nowhere to render today: `turn_start` carries a single `userMessage` and has no slot for a second one. Without a carrier, the person types something, the agent visibly changes course, and the transcript shows no reason why.

Add to the `SessionEvent` union in `packages/shared/src/session-stream.ts`:

```ts
| { type: 'turn_input'; seq: number; content: string; disposition: 'steer'; messageId: string }
```

with a Zod schema beside the neighbouring members, normalization in `session-event-normalizer.ts` so it is ingested into the OPEN turn (never opening or closing one), inclusion in log-backed history reconstruction so a steer survives in the transcript of runtimes that rebuild from the EventLog, and addition to the CLIENT EVENT ALLOWLIST. A new `SessionEvent` member that is not allowlisted is dropped silently; this has bitten before, and a steer that renders in dev and vanishes in prod is exactly that bug.

Client rendering: the steer appears inline inside the running turn as a user message, in reading order at the point it arrived, because that is what the person did. It is not a separate turn and must not look like one.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A steer emits exactly one `turn_input` on the durable stream, ingested into the open turn.
2. The turn's `turn_start` and `turn_end` counts are unchanged: one each, no matter how many steers it received.
3. Reconnecting mid-turn with `Last-Event-ID` replays the `turn_input` in the right position, gap-free.
4. A cold hydrate after the turn completes shows the steer inline in the transcript, in the right place.
5. The event is allowlisted: a client-side test asserts a `turn_input` survives the event handling path rather than being dropped.
6. Log-backed history reconstruction includes `turn_input` content.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P4] Wire the degradation ladder end to end and declare honest flags on every runtime
tasks.description:
Make an unsupported disposition degrade visibly instead of silently.

Implement the ladder in the dispatcher (which already has its shape from task 2.3):

```
steer -> runtime declares supportsSteer AND a window is open AND no pending interaction
           -> deliverIntoTurn({ mode: 'steer' })
         else -> queue
stage -> runtime declares supportsContextStaging
           -> deliverIntoTurn({ mode: 'stage' })
         else -> hold and fold into the next dispatch as an additionalContext entry
queue -> always available
```

Every downgrade emits a `queue_update` carrying the `MessageDeliveryOutcome` with `requested`, `applied`, and `degradedBecause` populated. The ONE case the UI must stay silent about is `degradedBecause: 'session-idle'`: the message ran immediately, which is not a degradation anybody needs told.

Declare the flags honestly:
- `claude-code`: `supportsSteer: true`, `supportsContextStaging: true`.
- `codex`: both `false`. Its adapter uses the SDK's thread API whose only interrupt primitive is an `AbortSignal`, and whether `@openai/codex-sdk` exposes `turn/steer` at all is UNVERIFIED. Before declaring, run a live probe against a real `codex` binary and record the result in `codex/NOTES.md` alongside the other live-verified facts. If steer turns out to be reachable, that is a follow-up task, not a scope expansion here; declare what you measured.
- `opencode`: both `false`. Interrupt is `POST /session/{id}/abort`, and the DOR-82 survey found OpenCode's queue lives in its own TUI rather than its server.
- `test-mode`: both `true`, deterministically, because it exists to exercise the contract.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A steer requested against claude-code with an open window is delivered natively; the outcome shows `requested: 'steer', applied: 'steer'` and no downgrade.
2. A steer requested against codex or opencode is queued; the outcome shows `applied: 'queue', degradedBecause: 'unsupported'`.
3. A steer requested against an IDLE session runs immediately with `degradedBecause: 'session-idle'`, and the UI stays quiet.
4. A steer requested while a pending interaction is open is queued with `degradedBecause: 'pending-interaction'` and does NOT fire into the open ask.
5. A stage requested against a runtime without the capability folds into the next dispatch and says so.
6. The codex live-probe result is recorded in `codex/NOTES.md` with what was run and what was observed. A declared `false` that was never probed is not acceptable.
tasks.activeForm: Wiring the degradation ladder and honest flags

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P4] Extend the conformance suite with the disposition, terminal, queue, and capability cases
tasks.description:
Hold every runtime to the contract, because a capability that is not conformance-tested is a capability a runtime can lie about. The suite already proves this discipline works: `validatePresenceReport` exists precisely so a runtime cannot fabricate presence.

Add to `RuntimeConformanceOpts` in `packages/test-utils/src/runtime-conformance.ts`:

```ts
  /**
   * Drives ONE turn to the point where it is OPEN, calls `midTurn`, then lets it
   * close. Required for the disposition cases; without it they SKIP by name
   * rather than passing on a manufactured absence.
   */
  dispositionTurn?: (
    runtime: AgentRuntime,
    sessionId: string,
    content: string,
    probes: { midTurn: () => Promise<void> }
  ) => Promise<void>;
```

Add four cases:
- **C1 disposition honesty.** For each of steer and stage: capability declared means the message reaches the model with no new `turn_start`; not declared means `deliverIntoTurn` is absent or returns `{ delivered: false, reason: 'unsupported' }`. Neither branch throws.
- **C2 terminal exactly once.** A turn window emits exactly one `turn_end`, however many native `result` messages the backend produced. PROVE IT CAN FAIL: remove task 0.1's idempotence guard, watch C2 go red, restore it, and record that in the PR.
- **C3 queue durability.** A message queued behind a turn that FAILS still runs; a message never runs while a pending interaction is open.
- **C6 capability completeness.** All three new flags present and boolean. Compile-time forced already, asserted anyway so a cast cannot dodge it.

Wire the drivers for all four runtimes where they apply, following the established stance: a case with no driver registers as a NAMED SKIP rather than passing on an absence the suite manufactured.

Update `contributing/adding-a-runtime.md` with the new capability flags, the ladder, `deliverIntoTurn`, and the new cases and drivers, written in the same voice as the existing presence-truthfulness section.

Acceptance criteria:
1. C1, C2, C3, C6 are green for claude-code, codex, opencode, and test-mode, with skips named where a driver legitimately does not apply.
2. C2's defect-seeded proof is documented in the PR description.
3. C1 is proved able to fail: declare `supportsSteer: true` on a runtime that cannot steer and watch it go red.
4. `contributing/adding-a-runtime.md` documents everything a runtime author must now declare, including the instruction to declare from MEASURED behavior rather than from a capability's name.
5. The full suite runtime does not regress noticeably; the new cases reuse existing harnesses rather than booting more.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P4] Build the composer's Queue / Steer / Add context affordances and the downgrade notice
tasks.description:
Give the person the three verbs, and never a dead button.

In the composer, the primary action offers Queue (the default) with Steer and Add context beside it. When the session is idle every disposition means 'run it now', so the split action collapses to a plain Send: offering three ways to do the same thing is noise.

Steer and Add context are HIDDEN, not disabled, when the resolved runtime does not declare the capability. A hidden affordance is honest; a dead one invites the person to wonder what they did wrong. This follows the repo's existing stance that a runtime with a missing capability adapts the UI rather than showing something that does nothing.

The downgrade notice: when an outcome carries `degradedBecause`, the queue chip says what happened, once, in plain words. 'Queued. Codex can't take messages mid-turn.' Never a code, never a field name. The `session-idle` reason renders NOTHING.

A steer renders inline inside the running turn (the `turn_input` event from task 4.3) as a user message at the point it arrived. A staged message renders as a quiet transcript entry, visibly not a turn.

Keyboard: Steer and Add context need shortcuts consistent with the existing composer bindings, documented in `docs/guides/keyboard-shortcuts.mdx` and `contributing/keyboard-shortcuts.md`.

All copy follows the `writing-for-humans` standard: plain enough for a smart 9th grader who does not code. Describe what happens for the person, never the mechanism.

Acceptance criteria:
1. On an idle session the composer shows a plain Send; on a busy session it shows Queue plus the supported extras.
2. Against codex or opencode, Steer and Add context are ABSENT, not greyed out.
3. A steer renders inline inside the live turn, in reading order.
4. A downgraded steer shows its notice once on the chip, in plain words, and the `session-idle` case shows nothing at all.
5. The dev playground carries a showcase for the new composer states (idle, busy-with-steer, busy-without-steer, downgraded chip).
6. Every changed component's full test set runs, including the tests of parents that mount it, not just the component's own suite.
7. Keyboard shortcuts are documented in both the user guide and the contributing guide.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P4] Make Stop clear the queue and hand the messages back
tasks.description:
Make Stop mean what a person thinks it means, without destroying anything they typed.

Today `POST /api/sessions/:id/interrupt` calls `runtime.interruptQuery` and answers `{ ok }` best effort. With a queue, a person who presses Stop and then watches the next queued message fire has been lied to.

Decision: Stop means stop everything queued. The SDK's own documentation names this exact case, describing `cancel_queued: true` as what a remote UI's Stop button sets so one round trip halts the session.

Implement:
1. Stop clears the DorkOS queue for the session, and `clear` RETURNS the removed rows (task 2.2 built it that way for this reason).
2. The cleared messages go back to the person: they land in the composer's draft area, the same promise `restore` makes today. Nothing typed is destroyed by a stop. This is the whole point of the task.
3. Pass `cancel_queued: true` to the runtime where the capability is advertised. Feature-detect it from `interrupt_cancel_queued_v1` in the `system/init` capabilities array; never version-sniff. A CLI that does not advertise it gets the documented older behavior, where queued commands SURVIVE the interrupt, and the person is told that honestly rather than being promised a stop that did not happen.
4. The confirmation names the cost before it happens: 'Stop, and put 3 queued messages back?' A confirmation that hides the consequence is not a confirmation.
5. Emit `queue_update` with the now-empty queue so every window agrees.

Honest reporting of exactly what was cancelled depends on the interrupt receipt, which is owned by the `runtime-interrupt-receipts` spec. Until that lands, the client says 'stop requested' rather than 'stopped'. Consume that spec's typed result when it exists; do NOT redefine it here.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Stop with three messages queued clears all three and returns their text to the composer, in order, and nothing is lost.
2. Stop with an empty queue behaves exactly as today, with no confirmation dialog for a queue that does not exist.
3. The confirmation names the message count.
4. Every window sees the queue empty via `queue_update`.
5. Against a CLI that does not advertise `interrupt_cancel_queued_v1`, the DorkOS queue is still cleared and the client does not claim more than happened.
6. Stop mid-turn still ends the turn; the queue behavior is additive and does not regress the existing interrupt path.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P4] Write ADR-a (three message dispositions at the AgentRuntime boundary)
tasks.description:
Record the contract decision.

Write the ADR at `decisions/<timestamp-id>-message-dispositions-at-the-runtime-boundary.md` using an id from `.claude/scripts/id.ts`, and add its `decisions/manifest.json` entry. Content:
- Context: `sendMessage` was the only ingress and `interruptQuery` the only mid-turn control. There was no way to accept a message mid-turn, no disposition, no steer. Concurrency was refused crudely at HTTP with a 409, and all queueing intelligence lived in the browser as ephemeral state. The industry has converged on queue, interrupt, and steer as distinct verbs (Codex models `turn/steer` separately from `turn/interrupt`; Amp uses a `{steer: true}` envelope flag beside a separate interrupt).
- Decision: three dispositions (queue, steer, stage) expressed ONCE at the server ingress as an envelope field, resolved by the server against declared capabilities, with interrupt remaining a separate verb because it carries no content and can be issued with nothing to send after it.
- Record the refinement that drafting forced, and why it is not a departure: a steer cannot ride `sendMessage`'s return type, because that returns an `AsyncGenerator<StreamEvent>` which the projector feed consumes as exactly one turn, and a steer's events belong to a turn another feed is already consuming. So the envelope stays single at the ingress and the runtime interface grows ONE OPTIONAL method, `deliverIntoTurn`, returning a receipt.
- Record the three capability flags and why there is deliberately no `supportsQueue`: the server always owns the queue, so every runtime supports queueing by construction.
- Record the degradation ladder and the rule that every downgrade is REPORTED. Silent degradation is the failure this design exists to prevent.
- Rejected alternative: three explicit required runtime verbs (`enqueueMessage` / `steer(turnId, content)` / `interrupt`). More surface for every future runtime author to implement, and it makes the common case (queue, which no adapter implements at all) look like adapter work.
- Rejected alternative: relying on the SDK's `priority: 'now' | 'next' | 'later'`. The field still carries no prose documentation at 0.3.224, so its scheduling is inferred from three words. Steering rides `streamInput`, whose behavior IS documented.

Acceptance criteria:
1. ADR-a exists with a timestamp id, is registered in `decisions/manifest.json`, and follows the repo's ADR shape.
2. Both rejected alternatives are recorded with their reasons.
3. The `deliverIntoTurn` refinement is recorded as a consequence of the type system, not presented as a change of mind.
4. A changelog fragment exists for the phase and passes the `fragment-present` gate.

tasks.phaseName: P5 — Default on, measure, clean up
tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P5] Run the flag-off versus flag-on measurement pass
tasks.description:
Produce the numbers that decide whether the default flips. The performance claim is the JUSTIFICATION for this whole programme, so it must be measured rather than asserted. Neither the ideation nor the spec made a performance claim; both marked the estimates unverified deliberately, and this task is where that debt is paid.

Run the same workload twice on one host, once with `runtimes.claudeCode.persistentSession` off and once on. A representative workload means a multi-turn session with tool use and at least one subagent, not a single hello-world turn.

Measure:

| Metric | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Time to first token, turn 2 and later | the `SESSION_TURN` span, already instrumented at the trigger seam |
| Cache-read token ratio | `cacheReadTokens` on the `session_status` the result mapper emits |
| Resident subprocess count | process sampling during a 20-session soak |
| Phantom-cancellation rate | the DOR-1087 tripwire counter from task 5.2 |

Expectations to confirm or refute honestly: TTFT materially lower from turn 2 (no spawn, no MCP reconnect), cache-read ratio materially higher, subprocess count bounded by `MAX_WARM_SESSIONS`, phantom rate zero. A refuted expectation is a finding, not a failure to hide: report it and let it re-open the design.

Also watch for LRU thrash: reap-then-immediately-rewarm frequency. If it is high, the remedy is raising the warm ceiling, NOT lengthening the idle timer, because a longer idle timer holds more processes for longer without improving the hit rate for the sessions actually in use.

Acceptance criteria:
1. All four metrics captured on both configurations, on the same workload and host, with the method written down so it can be repeated.
2. Numbers recorded on the work item, not just in a PR description.
3. Subprocess count under a 20-session soak stays bounded by `MAX_WARM_SESSIONS`.
4. Reap-then-rewarm frequency reported with a recommendation on the ceiling.
5. If any expectation is refuted, the finding is written up plainly and the phase does not proceed to 5.3 until it is resolved.

tasks.phaseName: P5 — Default on, measure, clean up
tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P5] Keep the DOR-1087 phantom detector as an instrumented regression tripwire
tasks.description:
Keep the phantom-cancellation detector alive as a tripwire, and make it count.

DOR-1087's detector recognizes the CLI's interrupt sentinel written as a tool_result when the CLI cancels a pending tool call itself, and distinguishes it from a real refusal: a UI deny carries its own wording and an operator stop goes through `interruptQuery`, so a sentinel matching neither is the CLI talking to itself. Observed on 2026-08-09: eight phantoms in one session, zero real denies.

The HYPOTHESIS is that persistence removes this class entirely, because DorkOS stops racing the CLI's internal queue: with a persistent stream, DorkOS controls when messages enter it and holds dispatch until the turn window closes. That hypothesis is UNVERIFIED and must not be assumed. A detector that never fires is cheap; a silently returned phantom is expensive and would be invisible without one.

What to build:
1. Keep the detector on the persistent path, not just the resume path.
2. Add a counter and a structured warning log so the rate is measurable rather than anecdotal, and feed it to task 5.1's measurement.
3. Add a unit test that seeds a synthetic phantom (a sentinel tool_result with no matching operator deny and no recent `interruptQuery`) and asserts the tripwire fires. A tripwire nobody has watched fire is not a tripwire.
4. Keep the corrective-steering behavior only if it is still reachable; on the persistent path the correction may be unnecessary. Whichever way, make the choice explicit in the code comment rather than leaving dead machinery.

Acceptance criteria:
1. The detector runs on the persistent path.
2. A synthetic phantom fires the tripwire; the seeded test proves it can fire.
3. A REAL operator deny does NOT fire it; a real operator stop within the suppression window does NOT fire it. Both are tested, because a tripwire that cries wolf gets ignored and then it is not a tripwire either.
4. The counter is queryable for the measurement pass.
5. No behavior change on the resume path.

tasks.phaseName: P5 — Default on, measure, clean up
tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P5] Flip the persistent-session default on and write the user-facing docs
tasks.description:
Make the persistent path the default, once the numbers say it should be.

GATED on task 5.1's measurement supporting the change and on task 5.2's tripwire reporting zero phantoms over the observation window. If either fails, this task does not run and the design is re-opened. That gate is the point of the phase; flipping the default on schedule rather than on evidence would waste the measurement.

What to do:
1. Change the config default for `runtimes.claudeCode.persistentSession` to `true`. Because the field already shipped at `false`, this needs a NEW semver-keyed migration key strictly greater than the newest release tag, not an edit to the existing one: `conf` runs a key only in `(storedVersion, projectVersion]`, so extending a shipped key never runs for anybody already on it.
2. Respect an explicit user choice. Somebody who deliberately set it `false` keeps `false`; the migration backfills only the unset case.
3. Write the changelog fragment and the user-facing docs per the `writing-for-humans` standard: what happens for the person, never the mechanism. 'Agents now stay warm between messages, so replies start faster', plus the queue, steer, and add-context verbs, plus what Stop does to queued messages.
4. Update `contributing/architecture.md` with the pump and the server queue in the hexagonal picture.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A fresh install gets the persistent path.
2. An existing install with no explicit setting is migrated to on; an install with an explicit `false` stays off.
3. The migration is keyed above the newest release tag and the migration-safety guard is green.
4. The changelog fragment passes the `fragment-present` gate and reads plainly, with no hype and no internals.
5. User docs cover queue, steer, add context, and Stop's effect on the queue.
6. `contributing/architecture.md` shows the pump and the queue.

tasks.subject: [persistent-session-runtime] [P5] After a quiet period, remove the phantom detector and the retired resume machinery from the hot path
tasks.description:
Delete what the new design made unnecessary, on evidence rather than on assumption.

This is deliberately a SCHEDULED task and not a step inside another one. The temptation is to delete the phantom detector at cutover, on the reasoning that persistence should have removed the class. That reasoning is exactly the kind that survives unexamined, and a silently returned phantom is invisible without the detector.

GATE: the tripwire from task 5.2 must record ZERO phantoms across a real observation window on the default-on build, including at least one multi-subagent session of the kind that produced eight phantoms in one sitting on 2026-08-09. If it fires even once, this task does not run, the finding is written up, and the design is re-opened.

Once the gate passes:
1. Remove `messaging/phantom-cancellation.ts` and its tests, and the session fields that exist only for it (`operatorDeniedToolIds`, `interruptRequestedAt`) if nothing else reads them. Verify with `pnpm knip` after building dists, and verify-before-remove rather than trusting the report.
2. Audit the resume-path machinery and confirm it is still reachable ONLY from the recovery route. `resumeSessionAt` anchoring and the `isResumeFailure` retry are RETAINED deliberately: they are what the crash and cold-start path needs. What must go is any hot-path caller left behind. Do not delete them wholesale; a comment explaining why they survive is worth more than their removal.
3. Leave a note in ADR-b recording that the phantom class was closed and how it was confirmed, so the next person does not re-derive the question.

Acceptance criteria:
1. The quiet-period evidence is recorded on the work item: what was run, for how long, with what result.
2. Zero phantoms over the window, or this task does not complete.
3. Knip reports no orphaned code after removal, and every removal was verified rather than trusted.
4. Resume machinery is still reachable from the recovery path, with a test proving a crashed session recovers through it.
5. ADR-b carries the confirmation note.
6. `pnpm verify` is green.
